message:
## Vulnerability Digest

The 24-hour window was **2026-08-27 05:10 IST to 2026-08-28 05:10 IST**. Six relevant Ubuntu security developments were retained after freshness, source, product-match, and duplicate checks. The highest-priority item is **CVE-2026-53362**, newly added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; Canonical rates it High and still marks multiple supported Ubuntu kernel variants vulnerable.

**Finding 1: Actively exploited Linux kernel IPv6 memory corruption**

- Product: Ubuntu Linux kernel
- Issue: CVE-2026-53362
- Severity: High, CVSS 3.1 score 7.8 (Canonical)
- Summary: Incorrect IPv6 fragmentation accounting can let an unprivileged local user trigger an out-of-bounds write through a UDPv6 socket. CISA added the issue to its KEV catalog on August 27, confirming evidence of exploitation.
- Relevance: Ubuntu is explicitly monitored. Canonical marks Ubuntu 26.04 and 24.04 kernel variants, and some 22.04 HWE/cloud variants, vulnerable or work in progress.
- Source: [Canonical CVE record](https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-53362) and [CISA KEV entry](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?field_cve=CVE-2026-53362)

**Finding 2: Ubuntu PAM login-lockout bypass**

- Product: Ubuntu PAM on 18.04, 20.04, 22.04, and 24.04 LTS
- Issue: USN-8688-1 (no CVE listed in the notice)
- Severity: Not stated by Canonical
- Summary: PAM could incorrectly clear failed-login records when some services invoked the account phase without authentication, allowing authentication lockout restrictions to be bypassed.
- Relevance: This is a new Canonical security notice for the explicitly monitored Ubuntu platform.
- Source: [Ubuntu USN-8688-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8688-1)

**Finding 3: Ubuntu Perl memory disclosure, code execution, and denial-of-service flaws**

- Product: Perl on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
- Issues: CVE-2026-12087, CVE-2026-57432, CVE-2026-13221, CVE-2026-57433, CVE-2025-15649, CVE-2026-48959, CVE-2026-9538, CVE-2026-48962, CVE-2026-7017
- Severity: Not stated in the Ubuntu notice
- Summary: The flaws cover memory disclosure, incorrect regular-expression matching, denial of service, arbitrary code execution from crafted input, and credential-header exposure during cross-origin redirects.
- Relevance: Canonical published the package security notice on August 27 for the monitored Ubuntu platform.
- Source: [Ubuntu USN-8684-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8684-1)

**Finding 4: Ubuntu openCryptoki out-of-bounds read and privilege escalation**

- Product: openCryptoki on Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 LTS
- Issues: CVE-2026-40253, CVE-2026-23893
- Severity: Not stated in the Ubuntu notice
- Summary: Integer underflows can cause out-of-bounds reads, while unsafe symlink handling can let a token-group attacker escalate privileges or access sensitive information.
- Relevance: This is a new Canonical security notice for packages on the explicitly monitored Ubuntu platform.
- Source: [Ubuntu USN-8686-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8686-1)

**Finding 5: Ubuntu p11-kit denial-of-service flaws**

- Product: p11-kit on Ubuntu 18.04, 20.04, 22.04, and 24.04 LTS
- Issues: CVE-2026-13757, CVE-2026-18938
- Severity: Not stated in the Ubuntu notice
- Summary: Improper RPC-message and nested-attribute handling can let a local attacker crash p11-kit; the nested-decoding flaw applies to 32-bit systems.
- Relevance: This is a new Canonical security notice for the explicitly monitored Ubuntu platform.
- Source: [Ubuntu USN-8687-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8687-1)

**Finding 6: Ubuntu kernel security-update bundle**

- Product: Ubuntu Linux kernels, including Azure, Oracle, IBM, Raspberry Pi, GCP FIPS, and livepatch variants
- Issues: LSN-0121-1, USN-8643-5, USN-8644-3, USN-8658-4, USN-8666-3; multiple CVEs listed in the linked notices
- Severity: Not stated at the advisory-bundle level
- Summary: Canonical published updates addressing multiple kernel flaws across networking, Open vSwitch, SCTP, filesystems, cryptographic, storage, media, and driver subsystems. Some notices require a reboot, and USN-8658-4 notes an ABI change requiring third-party kernel modules to be rebuilt.
- Relevance: Ubuntu is explicitly monitored, and all named notices were published on August 27.
- Source: [Ubuntu livepatch notice LSN-0121-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/LSN-0121-1), [USN-8643-5](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8643-5), [USN-8644-3](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8644-3), [USN-8658-4](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8658-4), and [USN-8666-3](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8666-3)

**MongoDB ecosystem sweep**

MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, mongod, mongos, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations and libraries, MongoDB-owned alerts, CVE/NVD, GitHub advisories, CISA sources, and credible research were checked. No credible MongoDB-related vulnerability was newly published or substantively updated in the window. The August 26 Kubernetes Operator release did not present a qualifying security disclosure.

**Freshness notes**

Chrome, Fortinet, Zoom, Veeam, SQL Server, and several other candidates were excluded because their authoritative disclosures or material updates predated the cutoff, despite recirculation in newer secondary reports.

Immediate review is recommended for Ubuntu systems affected by CVE-2026-53362 because of the new KEV status and Canonical's remaining vulnerable/work-in-progress package states. Apply the other Canonical updates according to the deployed Ubuntu release and package inventory.
